## Overview

Date pickers allow users to select a single or a range of dates. Pickers are
used to display past, present, or future dates. The kind of date (exact,
approximate, memorable) you are requesting from the user will determine which
picker is best to use. Each picker's format can be customized depending on
location or need. The `DatePicker` component expects a `DatePickerInput` as a
child.

<Canvas of={DatePickerStories.SingleWithCalendar} />

### Simple date picker

The simple date input provides the user with only a text field in which they can
manually input a date. It allows dates to be entered without adding unnecessary
interactions that come with the calendar menu or a dropdown.

<Canvas of={DatePickerStories.Simple} />

### Single date picker

Use the single date picker when you want to pair a text input with a calendar
popover. Users can type a date directly, or open the calendar and select one.

<Canvas of={DatePickerStories.SingleWithCalendar} />

### Range date picker

Use the range date picker when users need to choose a start and end date
together. The first input is treated as the start date and the second input is
treated as the end date.

<Canvas of={DatePickerStories.RangeWithCalendar} />

### Skeleton state

Use the skeleton state while a date picker is loading or while dependent data is
being fetched.

<Canvas of={DatePickerStories.Skeleton} />

### AI label

The input also supports Carbon AI label decoration through the `DatePickerInput`
`decorator` prop.

<Canvas of={DatePickerStories.withAILabel} />

## Component API

### API Compatibility

This implementation keeps the prop surface close to the Carbon React v11
DatePicker API. Most existing props work exactly as before:

**`DatePicker` props:**

- `allowInput` - Allow manual date entry
- `className` - Additional CSS class names
- `closeOnSelect` - Close calendar on date selection
- `dateFormat` - Date display format (default: `m/d/Y`)
- `datePickerType` - Picker type (`simple`, `single`, `range`)
- `light` - Use light theme variant
- `locale` - Locale for date formatting
- `maxDate` - Maximum selectable date
- `minDate` - Minimum selectable date
- `onChange` - Callback when date selection changes
- `onClose` - Callback when the calendar closes
- `onOpen` - Callback when the calendar opens
- `readOnly` - Make date picker read-only
- `short` - Use short variant
- `value` - Selected date value

**`DatePickerInput` props:**

- `autoComplete` - Autocomplete attribute
- `className` - Additional CSS class names
- `decorator` - Decorator component such as an AI label
- `defaultValue` - Default input value
- `disabled` - Disable the input
- `helperText` - Helper text below input
- `hideIcon` - Hide the calendar icon
- `hideLabel` - Hide the label text
- `iconDescription` - Accessible description for the calendar icon
- `id` - **Required.** Input identifier
- `invalid` - Show invalid state
- `invalidText` - Invalid state message
- `labelText` - Label text
- `name` - Input name attribute
- `onBlur` - Blur handler
- `onChange` - Change handler
- `onFocus` - Focus handler
- `onIconClick` - Calendar icon click handler
- `onKeyDown` - Key down handler
- `pattern` - Input validation pattern
- `placeholder` - Placeholder text
- `readOnly` - Make input read-only
- `required` - Mark the field as required
- `size` - Input size (`sm`, `md`, `lg`)
- `slug` - Deprecated alias for `decorator`
- `type` - Input type
- `value` - Input value
- `warn` - Show warning state
- `warnText` - Warning state message

### Breaking Changes

**Import path.** Components are now exported under the `preview__DatePicker`
namespace from `@carbon/react`. Destructure before use:

```diff
- import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from '@carbon/react';
+ import { preview__DatePicker } from '@carbon/react';
+
+ const { DatePicker, DatePickerInput, DatePickerSkeleton } = preview__DatePicker;
```

**`onChange` signature.** The v11 component called
`onChange(selectedDates, dateStr, instance)`. `preview__DatePicker` calls
`onChange(dates: Date[])` — an array of `Date` objects only:

```diff
- const handleChange = (selectedDates, dateStr, instance) => setValue(dateStr);
+ const handleChange = (dates) => {
+   const [start, end] = dates; // format yourself, e.g. Intl.DateTimeFormat
+ };
```

**`onClose` signature.** The v11 component passed
`(selectedDates, dateStr, instance)`; `preview__DatePicker` calls `onClose()`
with no arguments. Read the value from your own state.

**No Flatpickr APIs.** `preview__DatePicker` is not backed by Flatpickr, so
nothing Flatpickr-specific carries over.

**What changed internally:**

- Removed Flatpickr dependency (~15,000 lines of code)
- Implemented native calendar using Temporal API and modern web standards
- Added shared state machine with Web Components implementation
- Enhanced keyboard navigation
- Improved accessibility

### Date picker `dateFormat`

You can use the `dateFormat` prop to change how the selected date is displayed
in the input. The default format is `m/d/Y` (MM/DD/YYYY).

Supported format tokens:

- `m` - Month (1-12)
- `d` - Day (1-31)
- `Y` - Year (4 digits)

```tsx
<DatePicker dateFormat="Y-m-d">
  <DatePickerInput
    id="date-picker-format"
    placeholder="yyyy-mm-dd"
    labelText="ISO format"
  />
</DatePicker>
```

### Date picker `datePickerType`

There are three supported variations of `DatePicker` in Carbon.

- `simple` will render a simple text input _without_ a calendar dropdown.
- `single` will render a single text input _with_ a calendar dropdown.
- For `range`, two `DatePickerInput` components will need to be provided as
  children.

```tsx
// Simple (no calendar)
<DatePicker datePickerType="simple">
  <DatePickerInput id="date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>

// Single (with calendar)
<DatePicker datePickerType="single">
  <DatePickerInput id="date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>

// Range (with calendar)
<DatePicker datePickerType="range">
  <DatePickerInput id="start" labelText="Start date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
  <DatePickerInput id="end" labelText="End date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

### Date picker `maxDate`

Limits the date selection to any date before the date specified. Dates after the
maximum date will be disabled in the calendar and navigation will be restricted.

```tsx
<DatePicker maxDate="12/31/2024">
  <DatePickerInput id="date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

### Date picker `minDate`

Limits the date selection to any date after the date specified. Dates before the
minimum date will be disabled in the calendar and navigation will be restricted.

```tsx
<DatePicker minDate="01/01/2024">
  <DatePickerInput id="date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

### Date picker `value`

Pass a string value to either the `DatePicker` or the child `DatePickerInput` to
initialize the selected date.

```tsx
<DatePicker value="04/17/2025">
  <DatePickerInput id="date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

## Architecture

### Modern implementation

This date picker implementation uses modern web platform APIs and has **zero
external dependencies**:

- **Temporal API** - Modern date/time handling (polyfilled for browser
  compatibility)
- **Popover API** - Native browser popover for the calendar dropdown
- **CSS Anchor Positioning** - Smart positioning relative to the input field
- **State Machine** - Predictable state management shared with Web Components

**Benefits:**

- 🎯 **84% less code** compared to Flatpickr-based implementation
- 📦 **~20-30% smaller bundle** size
- 🚀 **Zero external dependencies** to maintain
- 🎨 **Full customization** control
- ♿ **Enhanced accessibility** with comprehensive keyboard navigation
- 🔄 **Shared logic** with Web Components implementation

### State machine

The date picker uses a finite state machine to manage all interactions and state
transitions. This provides:

- **Predictable behavior** - All state changes are explicit and testable
- **Clear event handling** - Events trigger specific state transitions
- **Maintainable code** - State logic is centralized and documented
- **Framework agnostic** - Same logic used in Web Components and React

States include: `IDLE`, `FOCUSED`, `CALENDAR_OPEN`, `DATE_SELECTED`,
`RANGE_START_SELECTED`, `RANGE_SELECTING`

For detailed shared state logic, see the primitives package in
[GitHub](https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon/tree/main/packages/utilities/src/date-picker/primitives).

### Keyboard navigation

The calendar supports comprehensive keyboard navigation:

- **Arrow keys** - Navigate between dates
- **Enter** - Select the focused date
- **Escape** - Close the calendar
- **Tab** - Navigate through the date picker interface
  - **Single mode**: Input field → Calendar (when open) → Outside the component
  - **Range mode**: First input → Calendar (when open) → Second input → Calendar
    (when open) → Outside the component
  - **Shift+Tab** - Reverse navigation through the same flow
- **Page Up/Down** - Navigate between months
- **Home/End** - Jump to start/end of week

**Tab Navigation Flow:**

In **single date mode**, pressing Tab follows this pattern:

1. Focus on input field
2. If calendar is open, Tab moves focus to the calendar
3. Tab again moves focus outside the date picker

In **range date mode**, pressing Tab follows this pattern:

1. Focus on first input field (start date)
2. If calendar is open, Tab moves focus to the calendar
3. Tab again moves focus to second input field (end date)
4. If calendar is open, Tab moves focus to the calendar again
5. Tab again moves focus outside the date picker

Shift+Tab reverses this flow, allowing you to navigate backward through the same
sequence.

When the calendar opens without a selected date, focus automatically moves to
today's date for easy keyboard navigation.

## Migration from Carbon React v11

### Import path

Import the `preview__DatePicker` namespace from `@carbon/react` and destructure
— the JSX stays the same:

```diff
- import { DatePicker, DatePickerInput } from '@carbon/react';
+ import { preview__DatePicker } from '@carbon/react';
+
+ const { DatePicker, DatePickerInput, DatePickerSkeleton } = preview__DatePicker;
```

Once destructured, usage is identical:

```tsx
<DatePicker datePickerType="single" onChange={handleChange}>
  <DatePickerInput id="date" labelText="Date" placeholder="mm/dd/yyyy" />
</DatePicker>
```

### Behavioral differences

1. **`onChange` signature.** Update handlers that rely on `dateStr` or the
   Flatpickr instance argument:

   ```diff
   - const handleChange = (selectedDates, dateStr, instance) => setValue(dateStr);
   + const handleChange = (dates) => {
   +   const [start, end] = dates; // format yourself, e.g. Intl.DateTimeFormat
   + };
   ```

2. **`onClose` signature.** Classic passed `(selectedDates, dateStr, instance)`;
   preview\_\_DatePicker calls **`onClose()`** with no arguments. Read the value
   from your state.

3. **No Flatpickr APIs.** Nothing Flatpickr-specific is available.

### Migration checklist

- [ ] Import from the `preview__DatePicker` namespace
- [ ] Verify you've accounted for the new behavioral differences
- [ ] No reliance on FlatPickr APIs

## References

- [Carbon React v11 DatePicker Documentation](https://react.carbondesignsystem.com/?path=/docs/components-datepicker--overview)
- The date picker uses the
  [Temporal API](https://tc39.es/proposal-temporal/docs/) for modern date
  handling
- The calendar uses the
  [Popover API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Popover_API)
  for dropdown behavior
- Positioning uses
  [CSS Anchor Positioning](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/tether-elements-to-each-other-with-css-anchor-positioning)
  for smart placement
- The `DatePickerInput` component takes in similar props to the Carbon
  `TextInput` component

Help us improve this component by providing feedback, asking questions on Slack,
or updating this file on
[GitHub](https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon/edit/main/packages/react/src/components/DatePicker/next/__stories__/DatePickerV2.mdx).
